headline: 7 commitments on Madurai's register: the Mullaiperiyar scheme delivered to all 100 wards, and 6 waiting - led by a High Court direction the state gave itself six months to meet.
intro: Dated commitments by the institutions that manage this city's water - the City Corporation, TN Water Resources Department, the state government and the courts that set deadlines for them - made to residents, courts and funders, and followed from announcement to delivery. Every commitment carries its original citation and every status change carries a dated source. Delivered late is still delivered - the dates show the journey - and when a date moves, the old one stays on the record. Nothing here is our opinion; it is the institutions' own paper, checked against time.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated timeline has not lapsed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: A public website of every Tamil Nadu water body - survey number, original and present extent - within six months (Madras HC, Madurai Bench)
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu, under R. Manibharathi v. Union of India, WP(MD) 31214 & 31221 of 2023 (Justices G.R. Swaminathan and B. Pugalendhi)
commitments.what: The case began with roads on the bunds of two Madurai tanks - Thenkal Kanmoi and Vandiyur Kanmoi. The bench used it to issue statewide directions on 7 March 2024: a dedicated public website listing every water body with survey number, location and extent 'both original and present', within six months (~September 2024); removal of encroachments; cancellation of water-body pattas issued after 1 January 2000. A portal exists at tngis.tn.gov.in/waterbodies (its assets date to April 2024). Our own live test of it on 5 July 2026 found survey numbers present, but only a single present-day area per water body - the original-versus-present extent that makes encroachment measurable is absent - two districts missing from the dropdown, and Vandiyur, one of the two tanks in the case itself, absent from the Madurai East and South village lists.

commitment_source.label: R. Manibharathi v. Union of India, order of 7 Mar 2024 (full text on Indian Kanoon); reported by SCC Online Blog, 14 Mar 2024

status_history.note: The state's own WRD Policy Note 2025-26 (p.39-40) says the court-ordered website 'will be extended to other districts of the State' - an admission that coverage was still partial around six months after the deadline had already passed.

Our live test of the TNGIS water-bodies portal: survey numbers are shown, but each water body carries one area figure only (no original-vs-present extent); the district dropdown omits Chennai and Mayiladuthurai; Vandiyur Kanmoi - one of the two tanks in the case - does not appear in the Madurai East or Madurai South village lists. No government statement linking the portal to the order, and no follow-up hearing, compliance affidavit or contempt petition, was found. Verdict: a website was stood up, but as of this date it does not meet the order's specification.
status_history.source_label: Neer Vazhvu live test of tngis.tn.gov.in/waterbodies, 5 Jul 2026

commitments.title: Mullaiperiyar 125 MLD dedicated water scheme (contract dates implied ~end-2023)
commitments.committed_by: Madurai City Municipal Corporation, under AMRUT with ADB TNUFIP Tranche 2 co-finance
commitments.what: Madurai's flagship supply project: a check dam on the Vairavanar at Lower Camp (Theni), a 125 MLD treatment plant at Pannaipatti, 144 km of transmission mains and 37 new overhead tanks, designed for 135 litres per person per day. The main contracts of May 2020 ran 30 months plus trial - implying completion around end-2023; press in September 2023 reported '95% of civil works' and a December 2024 deadline. CM M.K. Stalin dedicated the project on 7 December 2025, roughly two years behind the contract horizon. Tamil press reported ~30% of wards still without Periyar water in late January 2026; by June 2026 all 100 wards were on the scheme - but in rationed 2-hour ward-wise turns, not the design standard. Cost appears as Rs 1,020 crore (TNUFIP list), Rs 1,296 crore (AMRUT, DT Next) and Rs 1,653 crore (combined scopes) - we show all three rather than pick one.

commitment_source.label: ADB updated IEE for TNUFIP Tranche 2 (project 49107-005): packages awarded 27 May 2020, 30 months + 6 months trial

status_history.note: '95% of civil works complete'; deadline stated as December 2024; cost Rs 1,295.76 crore under AMRUT.
Dedicated by CM M.K. Stalin for 2.58 lakh families - about two years after the contract-implied date and a year past the December 2024 press deadline.

Post-dedication reality check: Dinamalar reports ~30% of wards still not receiving Periyar water. The article's own text ('1.5 months after the CM inaugurated') dates it to late January 2026; the page itself is undated. The pre-dedication MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 had recorded 160 MLD supplied against a 265 MLD requirement, once in 2 days in 86 wards and once in 3 days in 14.

The ward-coverage gap closes but supply stays rationed: Dinamalar reports the corporation running fully on Mullaiperiyar water across all 100 wards (2.5 lakh+ connections), supplied in 2-hour ward-wise turns - the live grievance being motor-theft leaving non-motorised homes dry. Reaching every ward is not the promised 135 litres per person per day; daily supply remains unachieved amid low Periyar/Vaigai storage.

commitments.title: Convert the whole city to 24x7 supply (81 zones) by June 2026
commitments.committed_by: Madurai City Municipal Corporation, under ADB TNUFIP Tranches 2-3 and the Smart Cities Mission
commitments.what: The corporation adopted a 24x7 supply model for all 100 wards: 8 zones under Smart City, 34 added-area zones under TNUFIP Tranche 2, and 39 core-city zones under Tranche 3 (813.5 km of pipes, 163,958 house connections, 115 new district metering areas per ADB's project document). The state's own policy note says verbatim: 'The project implementation period is between December 2022 and June 2026.' That window has now closed: the same policy note still records alternate-day supply citywide, the Smart City component sits at 86% on the corporation's own page, and we found no public evidence of any Madurai ward on continuous supply. One anticipated challenge, answered: the ADB IEE's line about '813 km of new distribution pipelines commissioned with 100% households connected' sits under 'Output 2... Works in Madurai include' - the 2022 planning document's expected-outputs list, not an achievement report.

commitment_source.label: ADB TNUFIP Tranche 3 IEE, April 2022 (project 49107-010); implementation window per MAWS Policy Note 2025-26

status_history.note: Three weeks before the window closes, CM Vijay orders officials to 'take steps to provide uninterrupted 24-hour drinking water in all 25 corporations' - a future-tense directive with no deadline, at a municipal-administration review. Madurai is not cited as done; companion coverage frames urban water upgrades on a five-year horizon.
status_history.source_label: Maalaimalar, 8 Jun 2026; similar in Daily Thanthi

status_history.note: The June 2026 window has passed. MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 records supply once in 2 days in 86 wards and once in 3 days in 14; the Smart City distribution component (15 wards, 35,000 connections, Rs 80.79 crore) shows 86% physical progress on the corporation's own project page, accessed this date. ADB's MFF availability period also ran to 30 June 2026, with no extension found.
status_history.source_label: Madurai Corporation water-supply project page, accessed 5 Jul 2026; MAWS Policy Note 2025-26; ADB Tranche 3 PAM

commitments.title: Underground sewerage for the added and left-out areas (Rs 502 crore, AMRUT 2.0)
commitments.what: Madurai's sewage problem is a collection gap, not a treatment gap: the state's own 2022 NGT filing shows 170.7 MLD of installed STP capacity used at just 39 MLD, and only 72 of 100 wards have underground sewerage. The fix is UGSS for the added areas - Rs 502.42 crore is MoHUA's combined AMRUT 2.0 sanction, which splits into components. The mission window closed in March 2026 (no known public extension order) with the project still at 'Contract Awarded' on MoHUA's own portal. On the ground the picture is 'laid but not commissioned': the southern expansion component (Rs 471 crore, 28 wards) has 215 km of sewers laid and tested with zero house connections and sewage still in open drains, officials citing prioritisation of the Periyar water project; the north-of-Vaigai component (Rs 275.82 crore, 308 km, 44,857 connections, built 'to prevent sewage discharge into Vaigai River') shows 17% on the corporation's page. No completion date has ever been published for any component.

commitment_source.label: MoHUA AMRUT 2.0 approved-projects portal (Madurai UGSS Rs 502.42 crore, milestone 'Contract Awarded'), accessed 5 Jul 2026; mission window per Union Cabinet approval of 12 Oct 2021

status_history.note: Dinamalar reports the Rs 471 crore expansion-wards component: 215 km of sewers laid and tested across 15 East-constituency wards, but not a single house connection given - sewage still flows in open drains, and Tirupparankundram has not begun. Officials blame prioritisation of the Periyar water project.

AMRUT 2.0's FY 2021-22 to 2025-26 window has closed with the project at 'Contract Awarded' (MoHUA portal) and the north-of-Vaigai component at 17% (corporation page, re-verified this date). No known public mission-extension order, though the Union Budget 2026-27 still allocates Rs 8,000 crore to AMRUT - funding continues, the deadline quietly lapsed. A government NIP portal entry claiming the Madurai UGSS was completed in October 2022 contradicts every official source above and is treated as erroneous.
status_history.source_label: Madurai Corporation UGSS page + MoHUA AMRUT 2.0 portal, accessed 5 Jul 2026

commitments.title: Vaigai River Front Development (Rs 84.12 crore, Smart City)
commitments.committed_by: Madurai Smart City Ltd / Corporation of Madurai
commitments.what: The Smart City riverfront: retaining walls, walkways, greenbelt, a Sanga-era theme park, lighting. The corporation's own progress pages tell the story: 85% physical in December 2021, 98% in July 2026 - thirteen percentage points in four and a half years, the full Rs 84.12 crore spend already incurred, the status still 'Work in progress', and the Smart Cities Mission itself closed on 31 March 2025. No inauguration of the full riverfront has been reported. The original sanction date and promised completion were never published; the register tracks what the corporation's own pages show.

commitment_source.label: Corporation of Madurai, Vaigai River Front Development project page; 85% figure per Wayback capture of 9 Dec 2021; Smart Cities Mission close 31 Mar 2025

status_history.note: Corporation's Smart City page (archived): Rs 84.12 crore, 85% physical progress, 'Work in progress'.
status_history.source_label: Wayback Machine capture of maduraicorporation.co.in, 9 Dec 2021

status_history.note: DT Next: the state 'has already spent approximately Rs 84.12 crore' on a riverfront 'said to be 98 per cent complete'. The corporation's live page, re-fetched 5 Jul 2026, still says 98% and 'Work in progress' - fourteen months after the mission that funded it closed. No inauguration coverage exists in English or Tamil. Meanwhile a successor has appeared: a new ~12 km riverfront tender (~Rs 80 crore) floated in 2026, and the Feb 2026 interim budget's Rs 374 crore five-city riverfront line includes Madurai - fresh riverfront money ahead of the old riverfront being declared done.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 13 May 2026; corporation project page re-verified 5 Jul 2026

commitments.title: Stop sewage flowing into the Vaigai (Rs 140 crore + Rs 440 crore proposals, unsanctioned)
commitments.committed_by: Corporation of Madurai (proposals to the Government of Tamil Nadu)
commitments.what: While Rs 84 crore was spent beautifying the riverfront, the river itself remains a CPCB-identified Polluted River Stretch. The corporation has two cleanup proposals pending with the state: a Rs 140 crore DPR (October 2025) to stop sewage entering from ~36 inlets, and a Rs 440 crore proposal (re-reported February 2026, with DT Next saying it has awaited sanction 'since 2024') to overhaul pumping stations and mains plus a new STP at the Panthalkudi canal. Between the two announcements the count of identified discharge points rose from ~36 to over 50. Neither proposal is sanctioned; neither has a timeline. Commissioner Chitra Vijayan, October 2025: 'Works will commence soon.'

commitment_source.label: Prokerala/IANS, 8 Oct 2025 (Rs 140 crore DPR); Hans India/IANS, 3 Feb 2026 (Rs 440 crore proposal)

status_history.note: The TN interim budget 2026-27 announces Rs 374 crore for riverfront development across five cities including Madurai (covering the Cauvery, Vaigai, Noyyal and Thamirabarani) and Rs 374 crore for sewage-treatment parks to prevent wastewater mixing into the Cauvery and Vaigai. State money formally announced near the problem - but not a sanction of the corporation's Rs 140 crore or Rs 440 crore proposals, and with no timelines.
status_history.source_label: TN interim Budget 2026-27, 17 Feb 2026, via Live Chennai budget highlights

status_history.note: Three months after that budget, DT Next still reports the Rs 440 crore river-ecology proposal 'awaiting Tamil Nadu government sanction since 2024' - a wait of two years or more. No sanctioned, dated Vaigai eco-restoration programme exists on the public record. (The Centre's June 2026 Rs 7,500 crore Urban Challenge Fund approval covers Chennai's rivers only; Madurai features in that mission under parks, not rivers.)

commitments.title: CM's December 2025 Madurai water-works package ('not mere announcements')
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu (CM M.K. Stalin, Madurai visit, 7 December 2025)
commitments.what: A named package announced alongside the Mullaiperiyar dedication: restoration of the Kesampatti village tank and Periyaaruvi channels in Melur (Rs 2.6 crore); lakes and canals in Kodimangalam, Melamathur, Pudukulam and Vilacheri (Rs 10 crore); the Uttankudi overflow-canal wall (Rs 7 crore); a new check dam near Balaaru, Surapatti (Rs 9.5 crore); and storm-drain upgrades in ~10 localities. The CM's words: 'These are not mere announcements... work will commence soon.' No completion dates were attached, and the amounts rest on a single outlet's report - both facts are part of this entry. No follow-up coverage of work starting had appeared by July 2026.

commitment_source.label: Tamil Oneindia, 7 Dec 2025 (single-outlet sourcing for the amounts; not yet corroborated by a G.O.)

update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked against a small calendar of documents: the MAWS and WRD Policy Notes each budget session (the state's own record of what it says it is doing), the MoHUA AMRUT 2.0 portal, ADB TNUFIP project documents, and the corporation's own project pages, whose percent-complete figures we archive on each check. Each commitment carries a next-check date; a passed next-check with no new citation is itself flagged, never silently updated.
sources_note: Sources are the institutions' own documents wherever they exist (court orders, policy notes, ADB IEEs, the corporation's project pages) and dated reporting where they do not. Where figures conflict (the Mullaiperiyar scheme's three costs, the sewage-inlet counts) all versions are shown with their labels. Claims that trace only to AI-generated aggregators or that we could not re-verify - a Rs 44.2 crore 'Vandiyur lake rejuvenation' that is actually a car park in the Smart City list, a '10-year Vaigai rejuvenation programme' - are excluded, and we say so.
